name: GPT family
context: Large context window; check the model page for the current size — it changes often.
pricingNote: Free tier in the ChatGPT app; API is paid per token. Live prices auto-arrive with the Phase 2 feed — check openrouter.ai/models until then.
strengths: huge ecosystem of tools built around it
weaknesses: can be confidently wrong — verify facts
bestFor: The safe default when you're not sure what to pick — the ecosystem around GPT models means almost every tool integrates with them.

name: Claude family
context: Known for very large context windows — long-document work is a signature use.
pricingNote: Free tier in the claude.ai app; API is paid per token. Live prices auto-arrive with the Phase 2 feed.
weaknesses: less third-party tool coverage than GPT
bestFor: Long documents, careful writing, and coding — try it when an answer needs to actually be read by humans.

name: Gemini family
context: Very large context windows are a family trait — some variants ingest entire books and video.
pricingNote: Generous free tiers in both the app and AI Studio. Live prices auto-arrive with the Phase 2 feed.
weaknesses: answers can feel inconsistent between versions
bestFor: Multimodal work (video understanding, screenshots) and anyone living in Google Docs/Sheets/Gmail.

name: GLM family
context: Competitive context sizes; some variants specialized for coding and agent workflows.
pricingNote: Known for aggressive pricing vs the big labs, with some open-weight releases. Live prices auto-arrive with the Phase 2 feed.
bestFor: Budget API projects and coding assistants; the open-weight versions make it a serious local-AI option.

name: Llama family
context: Varies by size; the small variants are designed to run on normal laptops.
pricingNote: The weights are free to download — running them locally costs nothing but RAM. Hosted versions cost per token (Phase 2 feed covers prices).
weaknesses: Behind the best closed models in raw quality
licensing has conditions for big commercial use
bestFor: Local, private, offline AI with Ollama — the 'ollama run llama3.2' experience is the on-ramp for a reason.

name: DeepSeek family
context: Large contexts; reasoning-oriented variants are the family's fame.
pricingNote: Made its name on extremely low API prices. Live prices auto-arrive with the Phase 2 feed.
weaknesses: multimodal support behind the big closed labs
bestFor: Cheap, good-quality API usage for text-heavy projects — and a benchmark for 'do I really need the expensive model?'

name: Qwen family
context: Varies by size; the many sizes make it flexible for local use.
pricingNote: Open weights free to run locally; cloud API is paid per token (Phase 2 feed covers prices).
strengths: Huge range of sizes and specialties
weaknesses: So many variants it's hard to pick
app experience outside Asia is limited
bestFor: Local models on modest hardware and multilingual projects — one of the best 'small model' lineups.
